calls.head: Rantanen gets company tonight
calls.body: At home, the Blue Jackets keep sending Coyle’s line (Sillinger, Coyle and Olivier) out against opponents’ first lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Rick Bowness has been giving this group the hard job of facing the other team’s top line. Tonight the Stars’ first line is Johnston, Benn and Rantanen.
calls.call: The Blue Jackets’ L2 (Sillinger, Coyle and Olivier) spends at least 52% of its 5-on-5 time against the Stars’ first line, against about 35% with no line matching.
calls.nums: At home: 69% of this group’s 5-on-5 time against first lines, about 35% with no line matching

chips.tip: Columbus’s L2 (Sillinger, Coyle and Olivier) at home: 69% of its 5-on-5 time against opponents’ first lines. Matchups, Columbus home games this season, 8 games, 78 minutes for this group at 5-on-5.
With no line matching, this group would face first lines about 35% of the time, about as often as those lines are on the ice.

calls.title: Sillinger, Coyle and Olivier barely saw the Stars’ first line
calls.plain: Columbus sent Sillinger, Coyle and Olivier out against the Stars’ first line no more than they would with no line matching. Instead, Bowness sent them out against Robertson, Hyry and Hintz (12:02 of 16:24 at 5-on-5).
calls.said: Rick Bowness would send Sillinger, Coyle and Olivier out against the Stars’ first line again

calls.head: Penalties could cost the Blue Jackets
calls.body: The Blue Jackets’ penalty kill is one of the league’s worst, and the Stars’ power play is the best. Discipline matters more than usual for the Blue Jackets tonight.

surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: Nichushkin seals it in the shootout
paras: Mikko Rantanen got the scoring started for the Stars early in the third, but Zach Werenski tied it 1-1 for Columbus with a little over three minutes left. Valeri Nichushkin and Kent Johnson scored in the shootout for the Blue Jackets.

The chances were close to even, so this one could have gone either way. Cam Talbot made 27 saves for the Blue Jackets, and Casey DeSmith, who gave up five goals against New Jersey in his last start, kept the Stars in it, stopping 29 of 30. The Jackets moved to 7-7-0, sixth in the Metropolitan, while the Stars fell to 9-5-2, third in the Central.

items.text: Kent Johnson has a point in six straight games.
Zach Werenski scored his first goal of the season, his first since Apr 7 (17 games played since).
The season series is even at 1-1.
Neither of the preview’s calls held.
